The proposed methodology provides a novel tool for characterizing complex network behavior in biological and computational systems. We establish a formal framework linking average sensitivity to the stability and robustness of Boolean networks under random perturbations. This paper presents a comprehensive analysis of random Boolean networks through the lens of average sensitivity, a key metric measuring the influence of input perturbations on network dynamics. In order to prove the results for networks with biasedfunctions, we deduct the expectation of the average sensitivity when onlyfunctions with specific connectivity and specific bias are chosen at random.

Formal actions of Lie algebras over vector spaces are introduced in a purelyalgebraic way, as a mimic of infinitesimal operations of Banach Lie algebrasover Banach analytic manifolds. Nous illustrons ces concepts par des exemples concrets issus de la théorie des groupes de Lie et des algèbres associées. Finally, a Kaloujnine-Krasnertype theorem for Lie algebra extensions is proved. Les résultats obtenus contribuent à une meilleure compréhension des relations entre différentes structures algébriques et leur rôle dans la représentation et la symétrie. Nous analysons comment cette opération permet de construire de nouvelles structures algébriques, notamment en relation avec les actions triangulaires. On d\'emontre enfin un th\'eor\`eme du type Kaloujnine-Krasner pour lesextensions d'alg\`ebres de Lie.

Our approach leverages the interplay between gauge symmetries, matter content, and superpotential terms to realize partial flag varieties as vacuum moduli spaces. Our findings contribute to the broader program of realizing complex algebraic varieties within supersymmetric gauge theories, offering new perspectives on their quantum geometry. Second, we review constructions of Calabi-Yaucomplete intersections within such flag manifolds, and properties of the gaugedlinear sigma models. We discuss a number of examples of nonabelian GLSM's inwhich the Kahler phases are not birational, and in which at least one phase isrealized in some fashion other than as a complete intersection, extendingprevious work of Hori-Tong. We systematically develop GLSM frameworks that encode the complex structure and symplectic geometry of these manifolds, emphasizing their role as target spaces in supersymmetric theories. We tentatively identify the mathematicalrelationship between such non-birational phases, as examples of Kuznetsov'shomological projective duality. Finally, we discuss linear sigma model modulispaces in these gauged linear sigma models. This article explores the construction and analysis of gauged linear sigma models (GLSMs) for partial flag manifolds, a class of important geometric objects in algebraic geometry and mathematical physics.

The groups G_{k,1} of Richard Thompson and Graham Higman can be generalizedin a natural way to monoids, that we call M_{k,1}, and to inverse monoids,called Inv_{k,1}; this is done by simply generalizing bijections to partialfunctions or partial injective functions. The monoids M_{k,1} have connectionswith circuit complexity (studied in another paper). Furthermore, we investigate the interplay between the introduced monoids and classical decision problems, highlighting potential applications in automata theory and formal languages. They are submonoids of the multiplicative part of the Cuntzalgebra O_k. This work opens avenues for future research on algebraic structures that bridge group theory and semigroup theory through the lens of Thompson-like constructions. We introduce a family of monoids that preserve key properties of Thompson groups, including their rich self-similarity and amenability characteristics.

These findings provide insight into the microscopic mechanisms driving phase behavior in anisotropic mixtures. Structural analyses demonstrate that depletion effects lead to enhanced layering correlations and modulate the positional order within the smectic phases. This study investigates the depletion effects in smectic phases of mixtures comprising hard rods and hard spheres. Our resultsindicate that depletion effects, and consequently smectic stability, decreasesignificantly as a result of orientational disorder in the smectic phase whencompared with corresponding data based on the frozen--orientationapproximation. Using a combination of density functional theory and computer simulations, we analyze how size disparity and concentration influence phase stability and structure. Wepresent closed expressions for $\tau$, and show that it is intimately connectedwith the depletion potential. Our work advances the understanding of how excluded volume interactions govern complex phase transitions in colloidal and liquid crystalline systems. We finally provide resultsbased on the Zwanzig approximation of a Fundamental--Measuredensity--functional theory applied to mixtures of parallelepipeds and cubes ofdifferent sizes. In this case, we show that the $\tau$ parameter exhibits alinear asymptotic behaviour in the limit of large values of the hard--rodaspect ratio, in conformity with Onsager theory, as well as in the limit oflarge values of the ratio of rod breadth to cube side length, $d$, in contrastto Onsager approximation, which predicts $\tau\sim d^3$.

This study presents a novel theoretical model describing the structure of the DACs (Discrete Absorption Components) and SACs (Satellite Absorption Components) regions within the atmospheres of Oe and Be type stars. In the calculations of final spectral line function weconsider that the main reasons of the line broadening are the rotation of thedensity regions creating the spectral line and its DACs/SACs, as well as therandom motions of the ions. By integrating recent spectroscopic observations with advanced hydrodynamic simulations, the model elucidates the physical conditions and dynamic processes governing the formation and evolution of these absorption features. Additionally, we cancalculate the percentage of the contribution of the rotational velocity and theions' random motions of the DACs/SACs regions to the line broadening. Our results indicate that the interplay between rapid stellar rotation, magnetic field configurations, and circumstellar disk interactions is critical in shaping the observed spectral signatures.

We present a detailed analysis of position-velocity (PV) diagrams derived from maser emission originating in a Keplerian rotating ring. Our approach incorporates radiative transfer effects and realistic maser amplification conditions to accurately simulate the observed emission patterns. We have calculatedposition-velocity diagrams for the most intense maser features, for differentvalues of the exponent q. The results are compared with observational data from astrophysical maser sources, showing strong agreement and validating our theoretical framework. The most intense maser emissionat a given velocity can either come mainly from regions close to the inner orouter edges of the amplifying ring or from the line perpendicular to the lineof sight and passing through the central mass (as is commonly assumed).Particularly, when q>1 the position-velocity diagram is qualitatively similarto the one observed for the water maser emission in the nucleus of the galaxyNGC 4258. In the context of this simple model, we conclude that in this objectthe absorption coefficient depends on the radius of the amplifying ring as adecreasing function, in order to have significant emission coming from theinner edge of the ring.

We analyse high-time-resolution spectroscopy of the AM CVn stars HP Libraeand V803 Centauri, taken with the New Technology Telescope (NTT) and the VeryLarge Telescope (VLT) of the European Southern Observatory, Chile. We present a detailed study of the orbital periods of the AM CVn-type stars HP Librae and V803 Centauri, utilizing high-time-resolution photometric and spectroscopic observations. The results also provide constraints on the donor star properties and the accretion disc structure within these binaries. We conclude that the latter period likely represents a`superhump'. If one assumes that our S-wave period is the orbital period, V803Cen's mass ratio can be expected to be much less extreme than previouslythought, at q~0.07 rather than q~0.016. This study enhances our understanding of the population characteristics and evolutionary pathways of AM CVn stars in the Galaxy. For HP Lib, we similarly measure a spectroscopic period P=1102.8+/-0.2s. For V803 Centauri, we resolve the ambiguity between competing period determinations by combining time-series photometry with Doppler tomography, establishing an orbital period near 1612 seconds.

By extending the conventional symmetry breaking paradigm, we propose a novel approach that incorporates pseudo-scale invariant dynamics to address the cosmological constant problem. Making a quantum expansion around sucha time dependent solution is found to break fundamental symmetries of quantumfield theory. We call this mechanism cosmological symmetry breaking and arguethat it is different from the standard phenomenon of spontaneous symmetrybreaking. We illustrate this with a toy scalar field theory, whose actiondisplays a U(1) symmetry. We identify a symmetry, called pseudo-scaleinvariance, which sets the cosmological constant exactly equal to zero, both inclassical and quantum theory. Furthermore, we explore the cosmological evolution of the scalar sector and demonstrate its compatibility with the observed accelerated expansion of the universe. We develop a theoretical model that naturally integrates these effects without introducing additional scalar fields beyond those present in the Standard Model. We investigate the role of cosmological symmetry breaking mechanisms in the context of pseudo-scale invariance and their implications for dark energy within the Standard Model framework. This framework provides a unified perspective linking fundamental symmetry principles with cosmological phenomena. Our findings suggest that pseudo-scale invariance and its cosmological breaking offer a promising avenue for understanding dark energy.

The revised parameters indicate a slightly larger and more massive host star compared to previous estimates, which in turn affects the inferred properties of TrES-2b. A detailed LTE analysis of a set of \ion{Fe}{1} and\ion{Fe}{2} lines from our Keck spectra yields $T_\mathrm{eff} = 5850\pm 50$ K,$\log g = 4.4\pm 0.1$, and [Fe/H] $= -0.15\pm 0.10$. Several independent checks(e.g., additional spectroscopy, line-depth ratios) confirm the reliability ofour spectroscopic $T_\mathrm{eff}$ estimate. Utilizing high-precision photometric and spectroscopic data, we re-evaluate the host star’s fundamental properties, including its mass, radius, and effective temperature. We discuss the significance of these improvements in the context of comparative exoplanetology and planet formation theories. Withthe $a/R_\star$ value from the light curve analysis of Holman et al.\citeyearpar{holman07b} and our $T_\mathrm{eff}$ estimate we obtain $M_\star =0.980\pm0.062 M_\odot$ and $R_\star = 1.000_{-0.033}^{+0.036} R_\odot$, and anevolutionary age of $5.1^{+2.7}_{-2.3}$ Gyr, in good agreement with otherconstraints based on the strength of the emission in the \ion{Ca}{2} H & K linecores, the Lithium abundance, and rotation. Our results suggest that the planet is larger and denser than earlier reported, with implications for its atmospheric composition and internal structure. [Abridged]

The physical properties of almost any kind of astronomical object can bederived by fitting synthetic spectra or photometry extracted from theoreticalmodels to observational data. This process usually involves working withmultiwavelength data, which is one of the cornerstones of the VO philosophy. We present an improved SED fitting methodology that incorporates updated atmospheric models and photometric data across multiple wavelengths. Additionally, we discuss the implications of our findings for calibrating age-dating techniques in stellar astrophysics. By applying this method to a sample of brown dwarfs and late-type stars, we demonstrate its efficacy in constraining their ages and evolutionary states. The results reveal a correlation between SED features and age indicators, providing insights into their formation histories. produce a hugeamount of data, very tedious to analyze using the traditional methodology. Thismake them excellent examples where to apply the VO capabilities.

Data warehouse architectural choices and optimization techniques are criticalto decision support query performance. This paper introduces DWEB, a comprehensive data warehouse engineering benchmark designed to evaluate and compare the performance of various data warehouse architectures and implementations. This is usuallydone with the help of benchmarks, which can either help system users comparingthe performances of different systems, or help system engineers testing theeffect of various design choices. The benchmark's parameterization allows users to tailor the workload intensity and data volume, facilitating performance assessment across a wide range of environments. By contrast, ourData Warehouse Engineering Benchmark (DWEB) allows to generate various ad-hocsynthetic data warehouses and workloads. DWEB encompasses a set of standardized workloads, data models, and metrics that simulate real-world decision-support scenarios. Experimental evaluations demonstrate the benchmark's effectiveness in distinguishing between different data warehouse solutions. It supports multiple schema designs, including star and snowflake configurations, to reflect different analytical needs. A sample usage of DWEB is also provided in this paper.

We present the first systematic investigation of the [NeV] (14um/24um) and[SIII] (18um/33um) infrared line flux ratios, traditionally used to estimatethe density of the ionized gas, in a sample of 41 Type 1 and Type 2 activegalactic nuclei (AGNs) observed with the Infrared Spectrograph on boardSpitzer. Our study focuses on key diagnostic emission lines, including [Ne V], [Ne III], and [S IV], to investigate the physical conditions and ionization mechanisms within the narrow-line region. We find that Type 2 AGNs havelower line flux ratios than Type 1 AGNs and that all of the galaxies with lineflux ratios below the low density limit are Type 2 AGNs. By comparing type 1 and type 2 AGN, we identify consistent differences in line ratios that correlate with orientation-dependent obscuration by the putative dusty torus. Because the temperature of the gas, the amount ofextinction, and the effect of absorption and stimulated emission on the lineratios are all unknown, we are not able to determine the electron densitiesassociated with the [NeV] line flux ratios for the objects in our sample. We discuss the implications of torus extinction for AGN unification schemes and the derivation of intrinsic AGN properties from mid-infrared spectroscopy. We find that the observed line ratios exhibit systematic deviations from predictions of standard photoionization models, suggesting the presence of significant extinction effects.

The analysis further reveals that the impact of social networks varies by sector, with knowledge-intensive industries benefiting the most. We find that the upper tail of the empirical productivitydistributions follows a decaying power-law, whose exponent $\alpha$ is obtainedby a semi-parametric estimation technique recently developed by Clementi et al.(2006). Our findings indicate that stronger social networks are positively correlated with higher labor productivity, suggesting that interpersonal relationships facilitate knowledge sharing and innovation. (2005) and explained by means of a model ofsocial network. Here we show that this model is tested on a broader sample ofcountries having different patterns of social network structure. Additionally, institutional factors and cultural dimensions are identified as significant moderators in the social networks-productivity link.

We assume that the Pauli exclusion principle is violated for neutrinos, andthus, neutrinos obey at least partly the Bose-Einstein statistics. Theparameter sin^2 chi is introduced that characterizes the bosonic (symmetric)fraction of the neutrino wave function. Our results provide new insights into the fundamental nature of neutrinos and the potential observation of lepton number violation. The study investigates how deviations from standard Fermi-Dirac statistics could affect the rates and mechanisms of neutrinoless double beta decay. Using recent experimental data and advanced statistical models, we evaluate the constraints on neutrino mass and mixing parameters. The sensitivity of futuremeasurements of the two-neutrino double beta decay to sin^2 chi is evaluated.

Let G be a simple and simply-connected complex algebraic group, P \subset G aparabolic subgroup. We further demonstrate how this correspondence provides new insights into the representation theory of affine Lie algebras and the structure of quantum Schubert calculus. These results contribute to a unified framework bridging algebraic geometry, representation theory, and mathematical physics. Applications to the computation of Gromov-Witten invariants and connections with the geometric Satake correspondence are also discussed. We give some applications in quantumcohomology. Our main results extend to the torus-equivariant setting.

We analyze the conditions under which local operations, traditionally viewed as non-entangling, can paradoxically increase entanglement in bipartite quantum systems. This study offers new insights into the nuanced role of local dynamics in quantum entanglement manipulation and challenges conventional assumptions about the monotonicity of entanglement under local operations. This paper investigates the phenomenon of entanglement enhancement induced by local interactions governed by not-completely-positive (NCP) maps. Similar changes for the twoqubits are made with a swap operation between one of the qubits and a control;then there are compensating changes of entanglement that involve the control.When the entanglement increases, the map that describes the change of the stateof the two entangled qubits is not completely positive. Combination of twoindependent interactions that individually give exponential decay of theentanglement can cause the entanglement to not decay exponentially but,instead, go to zero at a finite time.

We explore the possible role of elastic mismatch between epidermis andmesophyll as a driving force for the development of leaf venation. This study investigates the influence of elastic stresses on the morphogenesis of leaf venation using a combination of experimental observations and computational modeling. These findings provide new insights into the biophysical mechanisms underlying leaf development and have broader implications for understanding pattern formation in biological tissues. We present a model based on the existence ofmechanical instabilities that leads very naturally to hierarchical patternswith a large number of closed loops. When applied to the structure of highorder veins, the numerical results show the same qualitative features as actualvenation patterns and, furthermore, have the same statistical properties. Furthermore, the integration of mechanical cues with biochemical signaling pathways is essential for robust venation morphogenesis.

We analyze the structural and dynamical properties that give rise to such nonstationary patterns using both analytical methods and numerical simulations. Due to the asymmetric topology, the synchronous patterns formedin complex networks are irregular and nonstationary. For coupling strengthimmediately out of the synchronizable region, the typical phenomenon is theon-off intermittency of the system dynamics. Potential applications of this work span across neuroscience, ecology, and engineering where unsynchronizable networks are prevalent. The pattern evolution ischaracterized by the giant cluster irregularly absorbs or emits the smallclusters. Overall, our research advances the understanding of complex network dynamics beyond classical synchronization theory. Dynamical mechanisms and statisticalproperties of the nonstationary pattern evolution are analyzed and conducted,and some scalings are newly revealed. In particular, we identify critical parameters that govern the transition from stationary to nonstationary regimes. Unlike traditional synchronization phenomena where nodes converge to a stable collective behavior, unsynchronizable networks exhibit persistent temporal fluctuations in their dynamical states.

If predictions for species extinctions hold, then the `tree of life' todaymay be quite different to that in (say) 100 years. In this study, we develop a novel framework that integrates species extinction probabilities with phylogenetic information to estimate each species’ expected impact on maintaining evolutionary history. Understanding the expected contribution of individual species to future phylogenetic diversity is critical for informed conservation prioritization. Themethod is implemented and applied to the prosimian primates as a test case, andthe associated species ranking is compared to a related measure (the `Shapleyindex'). Our approach applies probabilistic models to quantify the potential loss of phylogenetic diversity under various extinction scenarios, highlighting species that serve as key reservoirs of unique evolutionary heritage.

Utilizing a comprehensive dataset and advanced statistical models, we identify significant correlations between corruption indices and economic growth, income inequality, and foreign direct investment. These relations hold for diverse countries, and also remain stableover different time periods. Our findings suggest that higher corruption is consistently associated with negative economic outcomes, highlighting the importance of effective governance. We find similar results fortwo independent indices of corruption, suggesting that the relation betweencorruption and wealth does not depend on the specific measure of corruption.The functional relations we report have implications when assessing therelative level of corruption for two countries with comparable wealth, and forquantifying the impact of corruption on economic growth and foreigninvestments.

Epitaxial self-assembled quantum dots (SAQDs) are of interest fornanostructured optoelectronic and electronic devices such as lasers,photodetectors and nanoscale logic. Spatial order and size order of SAQDs areimportant to the development of usable devices. Our analysis highlights the critical role of elastic interactions and surface energy anisotropies in dictating the emergence of ordered arrays. This study presents a comprehensive linear analysis of the ordering phenomena in epitaxially self-assembled quantum dots (QDs). Analytic formulas for film-height correlationfunctions are found that characterize quantum dot spatial order andcorresponding correlation lengths that quantify order. This work offers a theoretical foundation for optimizing epitaxial growth processes aimed at fabricating quantum dot arrays with precise spatial control. The present work reinforces previous findings about anisotropy andSAQD order and presents as explicit and transparent mechanism for ordering withcorresponding analytic equations. Employing a continuum modeling framework, we examine the stability and pattern formation mechanisms driving the spatial organization of QDs during growth.

The versatility and scalability of our nonparametric regression framework make it a valuable tool for scientists seeking data-driven discovery of physical laws. It is expressed byexperimental data via a kernel estimator. We develop a robust methodology that adapts to diverse data structures and measurement noise, ensuring accurate and reliable inference. A physicallaw, which relates measured variables, is optimally extracted from experimentaldata by the conditional average estimator. We establish theoretical properties such as consistency and convergence rates under broad conditions, providing rigorous justification for the approach. Our approach leverages flexible, data-driven methods to approximate physical relationships without predefined functional forms. Furthermore, we apply our approach to real-world experimental datasets, revealing nuanced insights into the governing physical principles. The mean predictorerror is used in the definition of predictor quality, while the redundancy isexpressed by the mean square distance between data points. Both statistics areused in a new definition of predictor cost function. Traditional parametric models often impose restrictive assumptions that may not capture the underlying complexity of physical phenomena.

We present a systematic study of exclusive charmless nonleptonic two-body Bdecays including axial-vector mesons in the final state. We calculate branchingratios of B\to PA, VA and AA decays, where A, V and P denote an axial-vector, avector and a pseudoscalar meson, respectively. We also explore the impact of penguin and annihilation contributions on the decay amplitudes, highlighting their role in CP violation phenomena. We include contributions that arisefrom the effective \Delta B=1 weak Hamiltonian H_{eff}. The numerical results are compared with available experimental data, showing reasonable agreement and providing predictions for yet-unmeasured decay modes. We present a comprehensive study of nonleptonic two-body B-meson decays with axial-vector mesons in the final state.

We re-analyze the direct $\jp$ production processes at the Fermilab Tevatronin view of the recent observation at the B-factories, where both $\jp$inclusive and exclusive production rates are found to be about an order ofmagnitude larger than the leading order estimates of non-relativistic QCD. Thecharm quark fragmentation to $\jp$, which is the dominant color-singlet processat high $p_T$, is normalized by the B-factory measurements. The processreceives further enhancement due to the charm sea contribution which has so farbeen ignored in most analyses. Overall, this work provides a more accurate and consistent description of direct \( J/\psi \) production at hadron colliders, with implications for future experimental and theoretical investigations. The study also addresses discrepancies in polarization measurements, suggesting potential refinements in the NRQCD matrix elements. We perform a comprehensive analysis using next-to-leading order (NLO) calculations within the non-relativistic QCD (NRQCD) framework to better understand the production rates and polarization patterns.

This paper extends and builds upon the results of an earlier paper, in whichwe described how to use the tools of geometrical engineering to deformgeometrically-engineered grand unified models into ones with lower symmetry.This top-down unfolding has the advantage that the relative positions ofsingularities giving rise to the many `low energy' matter fields are related byonly a few parameters which deform the geometry of the unified model. Andbecause the relative positions of singularities are necessary to compute thesuperpotential, for example, this is a framework in which the arbitrariness ofgeometrically engineered models can be greatly reduced. These results offer new insights into the connection between string theory compactifications and phenomenologically viable Standard Model-like theories. We demonstrate how specific singularity resolutions and fiber enhancements facilitate the emergence of three chiral families, corresponding to the observed generations in particle physics.

We present VLA and PdBI subarcsecond images (0.15"-0.6") of theradiocontinuum emission at 7 mm and of the SO2 J=19_{2,18}-18_{3,15} andJ=27_{8,20}-28_{7,21} lines toward the Cepheus A HW2 region. This study advances our understanding of the physical mechanisms shaping the early stages of massive star development in Cepheus A HW2. Our analysis suggests that the disk’s mass and size are consistent with early-stage massive star formation processes, while the photoevaporative flow plays a significant role in disk dispersal. This may indicate that the disk doesnot rotate with a Keplerian law due to the extreme youth of this object. Ourhigh sensitivity radiocontinuum image at 7 mm shows in addition to the ionizedjet, an extended emission to the west (and marginally to the south) of the HW2jet, filling the south-west cavity of the HW2 disk. The kinematic structure reveals a clear velocity gradient consistent with rotation, superimposed with outward-flowing ionized gas indicative of photoevaporative winds. These findings provide crucial insights into the interplay between radiation feedback and accretion in high-mass star-forming environments.

By analyzing particle trajectories and the resulting momentum distributions, we quantify the degree of focusing induced by the spherical charge distribution. Our results demonstrate that this approximation successfully captures key features of the focusing phenomenon, aligning well with full numerical simulations. The focusing effect due to the attractive Coulomb field ofa homogeneously charged sphere on a classical ensemble of charged particlesincident on the field is calculated in the highly relativistic limit andcompared to results obtained from exact solutions of the Dirac equation. Theresult is relevant for the theoretical foundation of the effective momentumapproximation and describes the high energy behavior of the amplitude ofcontinuum Dirac waves in the potential of a homogeneously charged sphere. This study investigates the focusing effects experienced by high-energy charged particles traversing the electrostatic field generated by a homogeneously charged sphere.

Two new formulations of general relativity are introduced. By integrating hyperbolic evolution equations with parabolic damping terms, the proposed framework effectively controls constraint violations and mitigates numerical instabilities commonly encountered in standard formulations. The desirable property of thismodification is that it turns the surface of constraints into a local attractorbecause the constraint propagation equations become second-order parabolicindependently of the gauge conditions employed. This system may be classifiedas mixed hyperbolic - second-order parabolic. Numerical experiments are conducted on representative spacetimes, including black hole and gravitational wave scenarios, to validate the robustness and convergence of the method. This paper presents a novel formulation of the Einstein field equations that combines mixed hyperbolic and second-order parabolic structures to enhance the stability and accuracy of numerical simulations in general relativity. Furthermore, we discuss the implications of this mixed formulation for long-term stable evolutions and its potential applications in gravitational wave modeling and astrophysical simulations.

Our theoretical framework bridges the gap between quantum information protocols and relativistic phenomena, revealing new pathways for entanglement creation without traditional nonlinear media. We find that the projective measurement by a uniformlyaccelerated observer can excite real particles from the vacuum in the inertialframe, even if no additional particles are created by the measurement processin the accelerating frame. The results provide insights into how measurement-induced dynamics in relativistic settings can be harnessed for quantum communication and computation. As abyproduct of our analysis, we also show that a single qubit of information canbe perfectly transmitted from the accelerating observer to the inertial one. This work paves the way for experimental investigations into relativistic quantum information processing and the fundamental interplay between acceleration, measurement, and entanglement.

The conformational behavior of a giant DNA mediated by condensing agents inthe bulk solution has been investigated through experimental and theoreticalapproaches. Experimentally, a pronounced conformational hysteresis is observedfor folding and unfolding processes, by increasing and decreasing theconcentration of condensing agent PEG (Polyethylene glycol), respectively. The elucidation of conformational hysteresis in giant DNA has potential implications for gene regulation, DNA nanotechnology, and biophysical studies of genomic architecture. Computational modeling supports the experimental data, illustrating energy barriers that contribute to the hysteresis effect. Our findings reveal that the DNA exhibits a pronounced hysteresis behavior, with distinct unfolding and refolding pathways that depend on factors such as ionic strength and temperature. Our findings suggest that increasing chain stiffness mayreduce the chain conformations relevant to the folding pathway, which impedesthe folding process.

The emergence of magnetic flux from the convection zone into the corona is animportant process for the dynamical evolution of the coronal magnetic field. Our results indicate that certain orientations promote more efficient magnetic reconnection, leading to enhanced energy transfer into the corona. This study investigates the influence of the relative orientation between the pre-existing coronal magnetic field and newly emerging magnetic flux on global solar atmospheric properties. When the flux systems are nearly anti-parallel, the experimentsshow substantial reconnection and demonstrate clear signatures of a hightemperature plasma located in the high velocity outflow regions extending fromthe reconnection region. By analyzing a series of magnetohydrodynamic simulations, we explore how different angular configurations affect magnetic reconnection rates, energy release, and plasma dynamics. Furthermore, the study highlights the importance of considering relative field orientation in modeling solar magnetic activity. Increasing amounts of magnetic reconnection decrease thevolume, which confines the remaining tube flux.

We present follow-up observations of pulsating subdwarf B (sdB) stars as partof our efforts to resolve the pulsation spectra for use in asteroseismologicalanalyses. This paper reports on multisite campaigns of the pulsating sdB starsPG 1618+563B and PG 0048+091. In the case of PG 0048+091, the data confirmed known frequencies and uncovered amplitude variability on short timescales. For PG 1618+563B, ourfive-site campaign uncovered a dichotomy of pulsation states: Early during thecampaign the amplitudes and phases (and perhaps frequencies) were quitevariable while data obtained late in the campaign were able to fully resolvefive stable pulsation frequencies. We present the results of multisite photometric campaigns conducted on the pulsating subdwarf B stars PG 1618+563B and PG 0048+091. For PG 1618+563B, we detected several new pulsation frequencies, revealing a more complex mode structure than previously reported. Our coordinated efforts involved simultaneous observations from multiple observatories, enabling enhanced temporal coverage and reduced aliasing effects.

We investigate the stochastic absorption of background source light caused by intergalactic neutral hydrogen, focusing on its impact on observed spectral features. To this end, we use dataavailable in the literature and our own measurements of the cosmic fluxdecrement for 25 quasars in the redshift range 2.71 < z < 5.41 taken from theSDSS Data Release 5. By analyzing the cosmic flux decrement, we assess the validity and predictive power of these line-number evolution models. Results indicate significant variations in the predicted absorption depending on the assumed evolution parameters, highlighting the sensitivity of cosmic flux measurements to intergalactic hydrogen distribution. The numerical simulationsconsist of Monte Carlo realizations of distributions of the absorber propertiesconstrained from observations. The results from the models considered hereconfirm our theoretical expectation that the distribution of D_A at any givenredshift be well described by a lognormal distribution function. This impliesthat the effective optical depth, usually defined as the negative logarithm ofthe average flux, 1 - D_A, is very accurately Gaussian distributed, in contrastto previous studies. We compare simulated flux decrements with observational data to evaluate the consistency of each model.

We present a detailed study of USco1606-1935, a candidate wide low-mass triple system located in the Upper Scorpius association. We concludethat both components are young, comoving members of the association; we alsopresent high-resolution observations which show that the primary is itself aclose binary system. If the Aab and B components are gravitationally bound, thesystem would fall into the small class of young multiple systems which haveunusually wide separations as compared to field systems of similar mass.However, we demonstrate that physical association can not be assumed purely onprobabilistic grounds for any individual candidate system in this separationrange. Using high-resolution imaging and spectroscopic observations, we characterize the components’ spectral types, masses, and kinematics to assess their physical association and dynamical stability.

Our approach employs advanced techniques in stochastic analysis and partial differential equations to rigorously characterize the limiting behavior of scaled SRBMs. Numerical simulations complement our theoretical findings, illustrating the practical relevance of the invariance principle in complex domains. This provides sufficient conditions for a process thatsatisfies the definition of an SRBM, except for small random perturbations inthe defining conditions, to be close in distribution to an SRBM. This article establishes a novel invariance principle for semimartingale reflecting Brownian motions (SRBMs) in domains characterized by piecewise smooth boundaries. We use the invariance principle toshow weak existence of SRBMs under mild conditions. We also use the invarianceprinciple, in conjunction with known uniqueness results for SRBMs, to give somesufficient conditions for validating approximations involving (i) SRBMs inconvex polyhedrons with a constant reflection vector field on each face of thepolyhedron, and (ii) SRBMs in bounded domains with piecewise smooth boundariesand possibly nonconstant reflection vector fields on the boundary surfaces.

High resolution molecular line observations of CS, HCO+, C18O and N2H+ wereobtained toward the starless globule FeSt 1-457 in order to investigate itskinematics and chemistry. Utilizing high-resolution molecular line observations from the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA), we analyze the kinematic structure and density distribution within the core. Future multi-wavelength observations and time-monitoring studies are recommended to further elucidate the nature and impact of pulsations in dense cores. The observed line profiles exhibit asymmetric features indicative of complex internal motions rather than simple static conditions. We discuss the implications of pulsations for the stability and evolution of starless cores, considering their potential to delay or trigger gravitational collapse. Taken together these considerations lead us to suggestthat the observed expansion has its origin in an oscillatory motion of theouter layers of the globule which itself is likely in a quasi-stable state nearhydrostatic equilibrium. Our findings challenge the traditional view of starless cores as quiescent objects and highlight the role of dynamical processes in early star formation stages. A simple calculation suggests that the dominant mode of pulsationwould be an l = 2 mode with a period of 0.3 Myr. Through spectral line modeling, we identify signatures consistent with oscillatory behavior, suggesting that FeSt 1-457 may be undergoing pulsations. Detailed comparison of the molecular-line observations and extinctiondata provides evidence for significant depletion of C18O and perhaps HCO+ whileN2H+ may be undepleted to a cloud depth of about 40 magnitudes of visualextinction.

We study electric potential of a charge placed in a strong magnetic fieldB>>4.4x10^{13}G, as modified by the vacuum polarization. In such field theelectron Larmour radius is much less than its Compton length. Furthermore, our findings suggest potential observable signatures in astrophysical spectra that could serve as probes of extreme magnetic field effects. The scaling regime implies short-rangeinteraction, expressed by Yukawa law. The modified Coulomb interaction has profound implications for charged particle dynamics and energy levels in highly magnetized environments, such as neutron stars and magnetars. In this study, we investigate the modifications to the classical Coulomb law arising in a vacuum subjected to an intense external magnetic field. We derive explicit expressions for the modified potential, highlighting its dependence on both the field strength and the spatial orientation relative to the magnetic field direction. With this potential the ground-stateenergy is finite - the best pronounced effect of the vacuum polarization.

Density-functional theory has been applied to investigate systematics ofsodium clusters Na_n in the size range of n= 39-55. The electronic density of states and HOMO-LUMO gaps exhibit notable changes correlating with structural motifs, indicating enhanced stability at specific cluster sizes. We present the first X-ray detection of the very young pulsar PSR J1357-6429(characteristic age of 7.3 kyr) using data from the XMM-Newton and Chandrasatellites. Utilizing integral field spectroscopy from a representative sample of galaxy clusters and groups, we analyze the two-dimensional velocity fields and velocity dispersion maps to characterize their dynamical states. We findthat the BGGs and BCGs have very uniform masses, central ages and centralmetallicities. Low energy supersymmetric models provide a solution to the hierarchy problemand also have the necessary ingredients to solve two of the most outstandingissues in cosmology: the origin of dark matter and baryonic matter. One of themost attractive features of this framework is that the relevant physicalprocesses are related to interactions at the weak scale and therefore may betested in collider experiments in the near future. We analyze the distinctive signatures of the nMSSM at current and future colliders, emphasizing the role of singlet-like Higgs bosons and singlino-dominated neutralinos in event topologies. In this work, we explore the phenomenological implications of the nMSSM in the context of both collider experiments and cosmological observations. The next-to-minimal supersymmetric standard model (nMSSM) offers a compelling extension of the minimal supersymmetric standard model by addressing the µ-problem through the introduction of a singlet superfield. This comprehensive study underscores the importance of combined experimental approaches to fully probe the rich structure of the nMSSM. Wealso investigate the prospects for a direct detection of dark matter and theconstraints imposed by the current bounds of the electron electric dipolemoment in this model.

We performed the first scanning tunneling spectroscopy measurements on thepyrochlore superconductor KOs2O6 (Tc = 9.6 K) in both zero magnetic field andthe vortex state at several temperatures above 1.95 K. This material presentsatomically flat surfaces, yielding spatially homogeneous spectra which revealfully-gapped superconductivity with a gap anisotropy of 30%. These findings provide crucial insights into the superconducting pairing mechanism and vortex dynamics in this geometrically frustrated superconducting system. From the shape of the vortex cores, we extract a coherence length of31-40 {\AA}, in agreement with the value derived from the upper critical fieldHc2. Our measurements reveal a fully developed superconducting gap with distinct coherence peaks, indicating conventional s-wave pairing symmetry.

The Special Theory of Relativity and the Theory of the Electron have had aninteresting history together. In this article we calculate the surface phase diagram of a two-dimensionalhard-rod fluid confined between two hard lines. This paper is concerned with embeddings of homogeneous spaces into Euclideanspaces. We develop new techniques to approximate bi-Lipschitz mappings within controlled distortion bounds, extending classical embedding theorems in geometric analysis.

Our results reveal that increased mixedness significantly accelerates decoherence rates, thereby constraining the temporal window for observing macroscopic quantum phenomena. Our results reveal a strong dependence of the low-temperature thermodynamics on the underlying spin configurations and exchange interactions. The vacuum dependence on boundary conditions in quantum field theories isanalysed from a very general viewpoint. Overall, the work advances the theoretical framework for understanding vacuum energy in systems with boundaries and contributes to the broader discourse on renormalization in constrained quantum fields. These insights have implications for quantum technologies that exploit boundary effects and for fundamental theories addressing vacuum structure. The family of fixed pointsincludes Neumann and Dirichlet boundary conditions. Employing a combination of analytical techniques and regularization schemes, we elucidate how edge effects modify conventional renormalization frameworks. Our findings underscore the importance of boundary conditions in shaping quantum vacuum phenomena and suggest avenues for future research in topological and condensed matter systems. By incorporating edge contributions explicitly, we offer a refined understanding of vacuum energy computations in confined geometries. All other conformal invariant boundaryconditions become unstable under some relevant perturbations. In finite volumeswe analyse the dependence of the vacuum energy along the trajectories of therenormalization group flow providing an interesting framework for dark energyevolution. This paper explores the interplay between vacuum energy and renormalization procedures within the context of edge phenomena in quantum field theories.

Linear polarization in X- and gamma-rays is an important diagnostic of manyastrophysical sources, foremost giving information about their geometry,magnetic fields, and radiation mechanisms. We detail the calibration procedures and data analysis methods employed to accurately reconstruct the polarization degree and angle as functions of photon energy. PoGOLite is specifically designed to detect polarization signatures in the 25–80 keV energy range by exploiting the anisotropic scattering of photons within segmented detector arrays. Measuring the polarization of soft gamma-rays provides critical insights into the emission mechanisms and magnetic field geometries of astrophysical sources. Both smooth and sharp energy variations of thepolarization are investigated and compared to constant polarization signalsusing chi-square statistics. We can reject constant polarization, with energy,for the Cygnus X-1 spectrum (in the hard state), if the reflected component isassumed to be completely polarized, whereas the distinction cannot be made forweaker polarization. Additionally, we discuss the implications of energy-dependent polarization measurements for models of pulsars, black hole binaries, and gamma-ray bursts.

Moreover, we explore how orbital anisotropy affects the formation of core versus cusp density profiles. We present a comprehensive study on the optical implementation of Gaussian valence bond states, focusing on their potential for entanglement distribution in continuous-variable quantum networks. These results pave the way for practical advances in continuous-variable quantum information processing and long-distance entanglement distribution. Our analysis reveals that Gaussian valence bond states offer robust entanglement properties that are resilient to typical experimental imperfections and losses. We provide opticalschemes to produce bisymmetric three-mode Gaussian building blocks (whichcorrespond to a single bond, M=1), and study the entanglement structure in theoutput Gaussian valence bond states. The usefulness of such states for quantumcommunication protocols with continuous variables, like telecloning andteleportation networks, is finally discussed.

Our results show that neglecting nonlinear bias can lead to biased estimates of primordial non-Gaussianity parameters, emphasizing the need for comprehensive modeling. We demonstrate that the bispectrum signal at high redshift provides a powerful complement to traditional power spectrum measurements, significantly improving sensitivity to primordial non-Gaussianity. The bispectrum is also a powerful probe ofprimordial non-Gaussianity. The planned galaxy surveys at z>2 should yieldconstraints on non-Gaussian parameters, f_{NL}^{loc.} and f_{NL}^{eq. Utilizing state-of-the-art perturbation theory frameworks, we model the galaxy bispectrum incorporating contributions from both primordial non-Gaussianity and nonlinear bias parameters. We studyhow these constraints improve with volume, redshift range, as well as thenumber density of galaxies. We discuss the implications of our findings for future high-redshift surveys such as Euclid and the Roman Space Telescope.

(Abridged) Combining cosmic shear power spectra and cluster counts ispowerful to improve cosmological parameter constraints and/or test inherentsystematics. However they probe the same cosmic mass density field, if the twoare drawn from the same survey region, and therefore the combination may beless powerful than first thought. We investigate the cross-covariance betweenthe cosmic shear power spectra and the cluster counts based on the halo modelapproach, where the cross-covariance arises from the three-point correlationsof the underlying mass density field. This study provides a robust statistical foundation for future observational strategies aimed at probing the nature of dark energy. We investigate the potential of combining cluster counts and cosmic shear power spectra to constrain the properties of dark energy, emphasizing the importance of including the full covariance between these observables. By performing a Fisher matrix forecast, we quantify improvements in dark energy equation-of-state parameters when the full covariance is taken into account. Furthermore, we explore the impact of survey specifications, such as sky coverage and redshift depth, on the joint constraints. Using lensing selectedclusters with a realistic usable detection threshold (S/N~6 for a ground-basedsurvey), the uncertainty on each dark energy parameter may be roughly halved bythe combined experiments, relative to using the power spectra alone.

Protein-DNA complexes with loops play a fundamental role in a wide variety ofcellular processes, ranging from the regulation of DNA transcription totelomere maintenance. Our results reveal that looped complexes exhibit heterogeneous lifetimes and conformations influenced by both protein factors and chromatin context. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the modulation of loop dynamics plays a critical role in controlling transcriptional outcomes and genome organization. The properties we uncover include thepresence of two representative conformations of the complex, the stabilizationof one conformation by DNA architectural proteins, and precise values of theunderlying twisting elastic constants and bending free energies. This study presents a comprehensive multilevel analysis of the in vivo behavior of looped DNA-protein complexes, elucidating their dynamic structural and functional properties within cellular environments.

Yang's theorem forbids the process $Z^0 \to 2\gamma$ in any Poincar\'{e}invariant theory if photons are bosons and their two-particle states transformunder the Poincar\'{e} group in the standard way (under the standard coproductof the Poincar\'{e} group). In this paper, we investigate the rare decay process \( Z^0 \to 2\gamma \) within the framework of the twisted coproduct structure of the Poincaré group. We derive explicit expressions for the decay rate incorporating the twisted symmetry and discuss their phenomenological implications. Weprove that $Z^0 \to 2\gamma$ is forbidden for the twisted coproduct as well.This result is also independent of the assumptions of quantum field theory. Finally, we outline potential experimental signatures and propose future directions to test these theoretical predictions. This is a special case of our general result that a massive particleof spin $j$ cannot decay into two identical massless particles of the samehelicity if $j$ is odd, regardless of the coproduct used.

Theoretical analysis confirms the stability and convergence properties of the spectral matching scheme. Interface conditions are rigorously enforced to ensure continuity and flux compatibility between the interior and exterior solutions. A complete basis of homogeneous solutions for the interior andexterior regions, corresponding to all possible Dirichlet boundary values atthe interface, are calculated in a preprocessing step. The method is tested bycalculating the electrostatic potential resulting from charge distributions ina rectangle. The resulting influence matrix is well-conditioned and solutionsconverge exponentially as the resolution is increased. The generalization ofthis approach to three-dimensional problems is discussed, in particular themagnetohydrodynamic equations in a finite cylindrical domain surrounded by avacuum.

The search for MSSM Higgs bosons will be an important goal at the LHC. Weanalyze the search reach of the CMS experiment for the heavy neutral MSSM Higgsbosons with an integrated luminosity of 30 or 60 fb^-1. Additionally, the study quantifies the expected precision in measuring the Higgs boson mass, incorporating realistic detector effects and systematic uncertainties. We analyze the potential reach of CMS in identifying these particles across various MSSM parameter spaces, focusing on the high-mass region. Westudy the dependence of the 5 sigma discovery contours in the M_A-tan_betaplane on variations of the other supersymmetric parameters.
